question: What is the primary function of the autonomic nervous system?
explanation: The autonomic nervous system manages automatic internal functions like heart rate and digestion without conscious thought. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h1)

question: How do nerve signals travel from the central nervous system to target organs in the autonomic system?

options.A: Directly through the spinal cord grey matter
options.D: Through a single direct motor neuron

explanation: Autonomic pathways use a preganglionic neuron and a postganglionic neuron to connect the central nervous system to body organs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which part of the spinal cord is the origin for the sympathetic nervous system division?
explanation: Sympathetic preganglionic neurons emerge specifically from the thoracic and upper lumbar segments of the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h2)

question: A patient experiencing sudden stress and a fast heart rate has maximal activity in which system?
explanation: Sudden stress triggers fight-or-flight responses through the sympathetic division, causing an increased heart rate and body tension. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the main chemical messenger released by postganglionic fibers in the sympathetic nervous system?
explanation: Most postganglionic sympathetic fibers release norepinephrine to interact with receptors on target organs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h3)

question: Where are nicotinic receptors located within the autonomic nervous system?

options.C: Directly on the surface of cardiac cells

explanation: Nicotinic receptors are found at the synapses of autonomic ganglia where preganglionic and postganglionic neurons connect. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h3)

question: What happens to the digestive system when the sympathetic nervous system is activated?

options.A: Blood flow and enzyme production increase
options.D: Muscular tone in sphincters relaxes fully

explanation: Sympathetic activation diverts energy away from digestion during stress, which slows down gut movement and reduces secretions. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is the direct effect on the heart when a drug blocks beta-1 adrenergic receptors?

options.B: Decrease heart rate and force of contraction
options.C: Increase cardiac output and accelerate pulse

explanation: Beta-1 receptors mediate sympathetic stimulation of the heart, so blocking them lowers both the heart rate and its pumping strength. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h4)

question: Where is the enteric nervous system located in the human body?

options.B: Along the lateral borders of the spinal cord
options.D: Within the walls of the gastrointestinal tract

explanation: The enteric nervous system forms a large network embedded directly inside the walls of the gut. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following is a key feature of the enteric nervous system?

options.A: It can operate semi-independently of the brain
options.B: It relies entirely on conscious spinal commands
options.C: It only functions when parasympathetic nerves are cut
options.D: It controls voluntary swallowing in the esophagus

explanation: The enteric network contains local reflex circuits that manage gut movement without needing direct instructions from the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which brain structure is the primary master control center for the autonomic nervous system?
explanation: The hypothalamus brings together signals from the body, emotions, and hormones to oversee all autonomic nervous system functions. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h6)

question: What role do brainstem nuclei play in autonomic regulation?

options.B: Storing long-term memories of visceral pain

explanation: Brainstem centers like the medulla oblongata coordinate subconscious autonomic reflexes that control heart rate and breathing. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h6)

question: Which chronic disease is a leading cause of damage to autonomic nerves?
explanation: Long-term high blood sugar levels in diabetes frequently damage delicate autonomic nerve fibers throughout the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why might a patient with orthostatic hypotension feel dizzy when standing up quickly?

options.A: Immediate widening of blood vessels caused by the enteric nervous system
options.B: Complete destruction of all somatic motor pathways
options.C: Excessive parasympathetic output slowing down the respiratory rate
options.D: Failure of blood vessels to constrict and maintain blood pressure

explanation: Dizziness occurs when autonomic reflexes fail to quickly tighten blood vessels and raise heart rate when a person stands up. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h7)
